newsitem.title: UK: British MPs alarmed by ease of fraud against EU.
newsitem.headline: British MPs alarmed by ease of fraud against EU.

text.p: A British parliamentary committee expressed alarm on Wednesday over what it said was the ease with which European Union farm and structural funds could be defrauded.
The powerful all-party Public Accounts Committee also said it was concerned about problems in ensuring that EU countries paid the correct amount for membership in the 15-nation bloc.
It said in a report that the complexity of EU operations in these areas was frustrating both auditors and fraudbusters.
The report said that the EU's farming fund, which accounts for about half the bloc's 60.3 billion Ecus ($75.7 billion) of spending this year, was governed by more than 3,000 regulations.

"We endorse the view expressed to us that the European Agricultural Guidance and Guarantee Fund should be subjected to structural reform and to simplification," the committee said. "We urge the U.K. government to press for such improvements."
It noted that estimated irregularities in the fund had quadrupled in the three years to 1994 to reach 320 million pounds ($539 million at current exchange rates) that year.
The report said the structural funds, covering areas such as regional development, were difficult to monitor because of the huge number of projects involved -- currently more than 31,000.
There were "serious weaknesses" in management and auditability, and the EU Court of Auditors had difficulty checking that EU states were providing their share of the cost of projects, it said.
The report also identified problems in ensuring that EU member states handed over the correct proportion of the value added tax they collect to Brussels.

Under the complex system by which the EU is financed, about half its budget comes from VAT receipts. The EU commission has estimated fraud in the collection system at 700 million Ecus ($878.8 million) a year.
The committee endorsed the aim of the Court of Auditors of seeking simpler, but more secure arrangements for collecting EU revenues. ($1=.7965 Ecu, $1=.5936 Pound)
